protocol.cell_types: arithmetic: addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division, modulo
protocol.conditions: 2 surface pairs (minimal, comment) x 6 perturbations (empty, identity, heavy, collision, pass, reassign_same)
protocol.metric: Spearman correlation of pairwise Euclidean distances
protocol.engagement_criterion: P(any digit) > 0.5 AND >90% correct for meaningful measurement

key_findings: ALL 7 capable LLM configurations show transfer rho in [0.083, 0.289]
Biology ranges from 0.877 to 0.975 — a 3-10x gap
NK K=N-1 (maximally epistatic random landscape) gives rho ≈ 0.199, within the LLM range
Instruction tuning effect is model-dependent: increases rho for Qwen (+0.04 to +0.14), decreases for SmolLM2 (-0.05)
Neither direction of instruction tuning closes the gap with biology
The [0.08, 0.29] range appears to be a property of the TASK (language processing), not training strategy
Cross-family validated: Qwen (3 sizes) and SmolLM2 (HuggingFace) both in range
All models ≥98% correct with P(digit) > 0.99 — genuine task engagement confirmed

interpretation.core_claim: Language processing has fundamentally low behavioral transfer (rho ≈ 0.18), comparable to maximally epistatic random landscapes. This is 3-10x below biological systems and appears to be an intrinsic property of the task, invariant to model family, size (0.5-3B), or instruction tuning.
interpretation.implication_for_alignment: Behavioral testing under one set of conditions predicts behavior under held-out conditions with rho ≈ 0.18. This means fine-tuning evaluation, RLHF alignment checks, and red-teaming cannot guarantee safety across the full distribution of real-world conditions.
interpretation.what_this_does_NOT_say: This does NOT say fine-tuning is useless. Instruction tuning clearly improves task accuracy (98-100% for all instruct models). It says that BEHAVIORAL TRANSFER — predicting how a model will behave under novel conditions from its behavior under tested conditions — faces a fundamental limit.
